The chapter's only accent remarks are general: Tagalog dialect stress differences (7.2.7.1.1), 'development of contrastive accent in Pangasinan', 'the apparent innovation of phonemic accent' in Proto-Philippines (7.4), and 'Additional research is also needed on Philippine accent patterns, which may prove to be a highly significant innovation unique to the Philippine subfamily' (conclusion). Southern Binukidnon appears only in the Central Bisayan membership sentence and (as 'Binukidnon languages native to the mountains of Negros') in the Ata-of-Negros para…

sources.note: Nothing for Southern Binukidnon. The language is only named (p.3 list of newly documented languages; Map 1.8 key n2; p.39 fn.5 Negros Binukidnon = Bisayan; p.249 fn.21 / p.379 fn.19 *l > zero even next to /i/; p.273 fn.33 *h retained in codas; one etymon hiyag 'like').
